source_architecture_summary: A natural-science history explains how manipulating a material's internal structure changes large-scale performance, moving through invention, process, mechanism, production constraints, and applications.
feasibility_notes: Blueprint A examines thermal tempering of glass; Blueprint B examines encapsulated phase-change materials for thermal storage. Both replace steelmaking, named inventors, dates, furnaces, and source analogies.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: Researchers study how migratory shorebirds combine fuel, wind, season, and habitat cues when deciding when to depart a stopover.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Process, internal stress, property change, testing, and scale
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Brittle-material problem, heating and quenching process, stress mechanism, fracture consequence, quality controls, cutting constraint, bounded applications
blueprints.distinctness_notes: A behavioral ecology account of departure decisions and probabilistic evidence; no manufactured material, internal structure, heat treatment, invention, industrial scale, or property engineering.

blueprints.blueprint_focus: Microencapsulated phase-change materials store and release heat during melting and freezing, with tradeoffs in leakage, cycling, conductivity, and building integration.
blueprints.overall_reading_skill_family: Phase mechanism, encapsulation, system integration, lifecycle testing, and scale
blueprints.rhetorical_or_narrative_arc: Temperature-swing problem, phase-change mechanism, capsule design, composite integration, cycling tests, timing constraints, qualified use
blueprints.distinctness_notes: Uses reversible phase transitions and composite design rather than glass stress.
